text:
**Short answer:** For most people, the **BLUETTI AC180** is the best value because it lasts more than one night even with a heated humidifier. If you only need a small, cheap backup, the **Tenergy T320** is the one to look at.

## Picks

**1. Best value: BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh), about $474 with code AFF5OFF**
- It runs roughly 3 nights with the humidifier off and about 1.4 with it on ([BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)).
- Dealectric lists $499, or $474.05 with the code, tested 2026-10-21. PowerStationBench shows $449 on Amazon, so compare before buying.
- Dealectric's record doesn't state the waveform, so confirm it's pure sine with BLUETTI. Other sources treat it as CPAP-suitable.
- [Buy the AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link)

**2. Best overall, if you can spend more: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (1,024 Wh), about $700**
- Tested Watts rates it quietest (about 20 dB under 200 W), with a 10 ms UPS switchover and a roughly 49-minute recharge. It's good for about 1.7 nights with the humidifier on.
- The sources I have don't include a direct purchase link, so see the [Tested Watts review](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/) and the [BuyerSheet price table](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).

**3. Cheapest option: Tenergy T320 (300 Wh), $225.99**
- It's the only unit in Dealectric's records that is explicitly pure sine and lists CPAP as a use.
- Tested Watts' planning figure is about 320 Wh per night with no humidifier, so 300 Wh may fall short of a full night. It's better for travel or a short outage with the humidifier off.
- Recharge takes about 8 hours.
- [Buy the T320](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-t320-300wh-power-station) (affiliate link)

**If you want to expand later: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (286 Wh, about $279–299)**
- It's light at 10.4 lb and can expand to 858 Wh.
- Sources disagree on its runtime: Tested Watts says about 0.8 night, while Outage Power Guide calls it "multi-night." I'd trust the lower figure. Details are in the [Tested Watts guide](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/).

## Things to know
- **Check your machine's label for wattage.** CPAPs typically draw about 40 W, or about 90 W with a heated humidifier. The humidifier roughly doubles consumption, and turning it off during an outage stretches a charge the most.
- **Use pure sine wave AC or your CPAP's own DC cord.** The DC cord through the 12 V port skips inverter losses and adds about 10–20% runtime. Only use a converter your CPAP maker approves.
- **Look for a UPS/pass-through function (about 10 ms or faster)** so therapy continues if the grid fails while you sleep.
- **Jackery's product pages say its stations aren't recommended for medical devices** ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)). Ask your CPAP maker before choosing one.
- **Plan for two nights.** The formula is nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85. With a humidifier that's roughly 520 Wh × 2 ÷ 0.85, or about 1,200 Wh.
- **Don't plan on flying with these.** All of them exceed airline battery limits.
- This is general information, not medical advice. If you depend on CPAP, ask your provider about a backup plan.

If you tell me your CPAP model and whether you use the humidifier, I can narrow this to one pick.
